text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 5.3% today after US crude oil prices tumbled below $100 a barrel on news that Trump signaled openness to talks with Iran at the UN. The stock had surged 7.4% over the prior four trading days as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East kept oil prices elevated, but that premium collapsed Monday as traders saw a potential off-ramp to the crisis—lower oil prices mean lower feedstock costs for refineries but also lower margins on refined products.

Refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, near maximum, which usually favors strong margins when crude is expensive; the reversal of that dynamic—falling crude with demand still steady—removes the tailwind that drove the stock higher last week. The shift hinges entirely on whether diplomatic talks actually materialize or whether tensions reignite, making the stock highly sensitive to headlines from the UN meeting and any Saudi production updates.
